articles.excerpt: Release: datasette-arrows 0.1a0 Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats. I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it. Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot. Add the plugin to Datasette ( datasette install datasette-arrows ) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option: This screenshot is from Datasette's main branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release. Tags: datasette , projects

articles.excerpt: CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and…

articles.excerpt: Amazon Aurora DSQL now lets you create multi-Region clusters whose Regions are on different continents, such as US East (N. Virginia) and Europe (Ireland). Until now, the Regions in a multi-Region cluster had to be in the same geographic Region set. With intercontinental multi-Region clusters, applications on two continents read and write to one strongly consistent database. If a Region becomes unavailable, committed writes are preserved and applications keep reading and writing in the other Region. You choose the two peer Regions and the witness Region. Place your database close to users on each continent, or separate failure domains as widely as your resilience needs require. Intercontinental multi-Region clusters are available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL supports multi-Region clusters. To learn more, see Multi-Region cluster availability in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL permet désormais de créer des clusters multirégions dont les régions sont sur des continents différents, par exemple US East (N. Virginia) et Europe (Ireland). Les applications sur deux continents peuvent lire et écrire dans une même base de données à cohérence forte, et les écritures validées sont préservées si une région devient indisponible. Ces clusters sont offerts dans toutes les régions AWS où Aurora DSQL supporte déjà les clusters multirégions.
articles.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports multi-Region peering across continents

articles.excerpt: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing. When customers subscribe to a third-party product, they can share their contact information with the seller. This helps sellers onboard new customers, send deployment guides and setup instructions, provide technical support, and share product updates from the start of the subscription. Customers share their first name, last name, email address, company name, and country or region in the deployment contact information section of the AWS Marketplace procurement page. AWS Marketplace pre-fills this section from the customer's previous purchases, AWS Profile , or AWS account details where available, so customers don't need to enter it again for each subscription. Customers can complete or edit any field before they subscribe, and view what they shared on the agreement details page in the AWS Marketplace console. Sellers can view the customer's contact information on the agreement details page in AWS Partner Central, or retrieve it with the new GetAgreementContacts API to bring it into their onboarding and support workflows. Sellers of software as a service (SaaS) products can call the API to pre-fill their registration page, so customers confirm their details instead of entering them again. This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To learn more, see Sharing your contact information at subscription in the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide and Receiving buyer contact information in…
articles.summary: AWS Marketplace permet désormais aux acheteurs de partager leurs coordonnées avec le vendeur au moment de l'abonnement à un produit tiers, notamment leur nom, courriel, entreprise et pays. Les champs sont préremplis à partir des achats précédents, du profil AWS ou des détails du compte, et les vendeurs peuvent les consulter dans Partner Central ou via la nouvelle API GetAgreementContacts. La fonctionnalité est offerte dans toutes les régions commerciales où AWS Marketplace est disponible.
articles.title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing at subscription

articles.excerpt: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store has increased the default throughput limits for five API operations. For accounts that have turned on the higher throughput setting, the quotas have changed as follows, in transactions per second (TPS): GetParametersByPath (from 100 to 500 TPS) PutParameter (10 to 50) DeleteParameter (5 to 50) DescribeParameters (10 to 100) GetParameterHistory (10 to 100) Parameter Store provides powerful, hierarchical storage for configuration data. The higher quotas give more headroom to workloads that call these operations in bursts. Examples include applications that load configuration by path when many AWS Lambda functions start at once, infrastructure as code deployments that create or update many parameters, and cleanup jobs that bulk-delete stale parameters.
articles.summary: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store relève les plafonds de débit par défaut de cinq opérations d'API pour les comptes ayant activé le réglage de débit supérieur. GetParametersByPath passe de 100 à 500 transactions par seconde, PutParameter de 10 à 50, DeleteParameter de 5 à 50, DescribeParameters de 10 à 100 et GetParameterHistory de 10 à 100. Ces hausses visent les charges en rafales, comme le chargement de configuration au démarrage de nombreuses fonctions Lambda, les déploiements d'infrastructure as code et les purges en masse de paramètres.
articles.title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store raises API throughput limits

articles.excerpt: AWS Transform for migrations now recommends the optimized storage type and configuration for every server you migrate, so you no longer do it server by server. Building on recent storage assessment capabilities , AWS Transform's recommendations use each server's observed performance and capacity data to reduce overprovisioning costs and avoid performance issues after cutover. You see the expected cost before you migrate, and AWS Transform applies the approved settings automatically at launch. Recommendations cover Amazon EBS and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. For FSx for NetApp ONTAP, they include the file system layout and sizing. You choose whether to optimize for cost or for performance, and recommendations stay consistent from assessment through launch. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for migrations is available . To learn more, see the AWS Transform user guide .
articles.summary: AWS Transform for migrations recommande désormais automatiquement le type et la configuration de stockage optimaux pour chaque serveur à migrer, à partir des données de performance et de capacité observées. Les recommandations couvrent Amazon EBS et Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, avec le coût prévu affiché avant la migration et l'application automatique des paramètres approuvés au lancement. La fonctionnalité est disponible dans toutes les régions où AWS Transform for migrations est offert.
articles.title: AWS Transform supports optimized storage for server migration

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of buyer approvals. This lets you decide which AWS Marketplace purchases need sign-off, who approves them, and where approval happens. You can define buying policies for the conditions that matter to you, such as purchase amount, product type, pricing, and whether an offer is public or private. Additionally, you can choose to route each purchase request to the right place: the AWS Marketplace console, a chain of approvers by email, or your procurement system in Coupa or SAP Ariba. When you route approvals by email, procurement, finance, legal, and cloud governance teams can approve requests without needing to sign into the AWS console. They see the product, price, terms, and can approve right from their email. For example, you can route large software commitments to Coupa or SAP Ariba for review, send mid-size purchases to multiple approvers by email, and let low-cost or pay-as-you-go purchases go through without approval. When a purchase is routed to your procurement system, it follows your existing approval flows and gets a dedicated purchase order for cleaner spend tracking and reconciliation. With AWS Marketplace, customers can already choose which subset of available products their teams can buy, track each purchase with purchase orders, and require their employees to enter a purchase order when buying. Now, with buyer approvals, you can also control how each purchase is approved before making a financial…
articles.summary: AWS Marketplace annonce la disponibilité générale des approbations d'achat, qui permettent de définir quels achats nécessitent une approbation, qui approuve et où. Les politiques d'achat peuvent se baser sur le montant, le type de produit, la tarification ou le caractère public ou privé de l'offre. Les demandes peuvent être acheminées vers la console AWS Marketplace, une chaîne d'approbateurs par courriel, ou un système d'approvisionnement comme Coupa ou SAP Ariba.
articles.title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer approval workflows

articles.excerpt: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances, so operations teams can start tracking and resolving customer issues on day one without any setup work. New instances come with Cases connected to rules for setting SLAs, Customer Profiles for personalizing customer experiences, and Amazon EventBridge for triggering actions in other business applications when a case is updated. Administrators of existing instances can enable these integrations with one click in the AWS Management Console. Newly added case fields sync automatically, so admins don't have to update integrations each time they create fields. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon Connect Customer active Cases par défaut dans les nouvelles instances, avec des règles de SLA, Customer Profiles et Amazon EventBridge préconfigurés. Les administrateurs d'instances existantes peuvent activer ces intégrations en un clic dans la console AWS, et les nouveaux champs de dossiers se synchronisent automatiquement. articles.title: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances

articles.excerpt: AWS Transform now automates the tasks that prepare and validate your servers during a migration, before they move and after they launch on AWS. AWS Transform is the agentic AI service that speeds up cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction. With the new source actions capability, you can create actions and run them securely on your source servers at the right point in the migration, from the early stages through cutover. Post-launch actions complement this by automatically configuring and validating each workload as soon as it launches on AWS. Cutover preparation and validation are often manual, time-consuming tasks in large-scale migrations. Traditionally, migration teams log in to each source server to stop services and freeze database writes before shutdown, and then check connectivity, application health, and monitoring on each server after it launches. With source actions in AWS Transform, you define each action once, run it in bulk on the servers and waves you choose, and reuse it across accounts and migrations. AWS Transform manages these actions centrally, so you can reuse them across accounts and migrations instead of rebuilding them each time. You can monitor the status of each action and confirm your go/no-go decision before moving to the next step. Source preparation and post-launch actions are now part of the migration plan itself, so you no longer have to coordinate and run these activities by hand. This capability is…
articles.summary: AWS Transform ajoute des actions automatisées pour préparer et valider les serveurs source avant la migration, par exemple arrêter les services et geler les écritures en base avant l'arrêt. Une fois la charge de travail lancée sur AWS, des actions post-lancement la configurent et la valident automatiquement. Ces actions se définissent une seule fois, s'exécutent en lot et se réutilisent entre comptes et migrations.
articles.title: AWS Transform automates source and migration target actions to accelerate cutover

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a new serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents. OpenSearch Memory stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives useful memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions, so agents can recall prior decisions, earlier interactions, and user preferences without replaying the full conversation history to the model. Customers can give agents long-term memory without provisioning infrastructure or building separate extraction, indexing, consolidation, and retrieval systems. OpenSearch Memory stores the original events verbatim, makes them searchable within seconds, and asynchronously derives structured memories. It manages the full memory lifecycle, including extraction, embedding, indexing, consolidation (adding, updating, or skipping memories as new information arrives), and retrieval using keyword, semantic, and hybrid search. Customers control access with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for each memory store, with actor and session scoping, and can set expiration periods for events and memories. Because it is serverless, there are no clusters to provision, instance types to choose, or indexes to create, and capacity for extraction and search scales automatically. Amazon OpenSearch Memory is available today in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Regions. For pricing…
articles.summary: AWS annonce la disponibilité générale d'Amazon OpenSearch Memory, une capacité serverless d'OpenSearch Service qui ajoute une mémoire persistante aux agents d'IA. Le service stocke les interactions sous forme d'événements consultables, en dérive des souvenirs structurés et récupère le contexte pertinent entre les sessions, sans rejouer tout l'historique au modèle. Il est offert dans cinq régions : Virginie-du-Nord, Ohio, Oregon, Francfort et Tokyo.
articles.title: Amazon OpenSearch Memory is now generally available

articles.excerpt: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations within minutes. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and reasoning behind each suggestion. You can use the agent on any completed job run from the AWS Glue console, or from your own tools through the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server. The agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen goal and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job artifacts together to identify what is driving runtime and cost: too little parallelism, a skewed join key, memory pressure forcing spill, idle executors, or capacity provisioned beyond what the job uses. When cost and performance trade off, the agent improves the metric you chose while keeping any regression of the other within defined limits. The engine also checks best practices such as platform-level improvements like upgrading to a newer AWS Glue version or using AWS Graviton processors. Each recommendation is labeled by the area it modifies: infrastructure, Spark configuration, code, or data layout. All access is authenticated with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and logged in AWS CloudTrail. The Apache Spark Optimization Agent is available at no additional charge for AWS…
articles.summary: AWS Glue ETL propose désormais un agent d'optimisation Apache Spark qui analyse les exécutions de tâches terminées et fournit, en quelques minutes, des recommandations de coût ou de performance selon l'objectif choisi. Chaque suggestion est accompagnée des données de télémétrie et du raisonnement qui la sous-tendent, et est classée par domaine (infrastructure, configuration Spark, code ou disposition des données). L'accès est authentifié via IAM et journalisé dans CloudTrail, et l'agent est offert sans frais supplémentaires.
articles.title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for AWS Glue ETL

articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions. With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run, and point their applications at the router. The router prefers endpoints in its own Region, shifts new requests to healthy destinations in other Regions as errors rise, and returns traffic gradually after the local endpoint recovers. Existing endpoints, models, and containers do not change. Endpoint owners stay in control: an endpoint policy determines which routers in other accounts can use an endpoint, and an optional cross-Region traffic cap reserves capacity for the endpoint’s local callers. Each real-time response identifies the endpoint that served the request and the reason, and router metrics in Amazon CloudWatch show where traffic went. Cross-Region inference routing is available for real-time inference in 32 commercial AWS Regions, and for asynchronous inference in 25 Regions.…
articles.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI propose désormais un routage d'inférence inter-régions, qui redirige les requêtes vers des endpoints déployés dans d'autres régions AWS ou comptes lorsqu'une région manque de capacité ou devient défaillante. Le routeur privilégie les endpoints de sa propre région, transfère progressivement le trafic vers des destinations saines et le ramène une fois l'endpoint local rétabli, sans modifier les endpoints ni les modèles existants. Les propriétaires d'endpoints contrôlent l'accès via une politique et peuvent limiter le trafic inter-régions; la fonctionnalité est disponible pour l'inférence en temps réel dans 32 régions commerciales et pour l'inférence asynchrone dans 25 régions.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports cross-Region inference routing

articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced version 1.0 of ExtendDB, the first release of the open source Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter for production use. ExtendDB is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and runs on a database backend that you choose, so developers and infrastructure teams can run DynamoDB workloads in on-premises data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge without rewriting application code. ExtendDB 1.0 supports four storage backends, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. For local development and continuous integration (CI), the extenddb-dev container image and the @extenddb/dev npm package run a DynamoDB-compatible endpoint over SQLite, so you don’t have to set up an external database. ExtendDB is maintained by AWS, released under the Apache 2.0 license, and developed in the open on GitHub. To learn more, see the ExtendDB project page . To get started or contribute, visit the GitHub repository .
articles.summary: AWS annonce la version 1.0 d'ExtendDB, un adaptateur open source compatible avec l'API DynamoDB, prêt pour la production. Il fonctionne sur le backend de base de données de votre choix (PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra ou MongoDB), ce qui permet d'exécuter des charges DynamoDB sur site, dans des nuages privés ou publics, ou en périphérie sans réécrire le code applicatif. Le projet est maintenu par AWS, sous licence Apache 2.0, et développé publiquement sur GitHub.
articles.title: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0

articles.excerpt: AWS Transform custom now enables you to share transformation definitions (TDs) and their associated lessons across AWS accounts, organizational units (OUs), or your entire organization in AWS Organizations through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). AWS Transform custom is a capability of AWS Transform that performs transformations across your technology stack, including API and framework upgrades, migrations, and language translations. With this launch, you can share TDs as live resources rather than static copies, so consumers run the owner's latest published version by default while the owner maintains full control. As the TD owner, you select from four managed permissions ranging from execute-only (the default) to permissions that allow consumers to use your lessons, contribute lessons back to you, or download the TD. Lessons flow back to the owner only when the permission allows it and the consumer opts in. This capability is particularly valuable for platform engineering teams and AWS Partners who need to deploy standardized transformations across multiple accounts. A central team can create a TD once and share it organization-wide. This feature is available via the AWS Transform CLI and AWS RAM in US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Canada (Central) Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS Transform User Guide .
articles.summary: AWS Transform custom permet désormais de partager des définitions de transformation (TD) et leurs leçons associées entre comptes AWS, unités organisationnelles ou toute une organisation via AWS Resource Access Manager. Les destinataires exécutent la dernière version publiée par le propriétaire, avec quatre niveaux de permissions allant de l'exécution seule (par défaut) jusqu'au téléchargement. La fonctionnalité est offerte via la CLI et AWS RAM dans huit régions, dont Canada (Centre).
articles.title: AWS Transform custom now supports cross-account sharing of transformation definitions

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs. You can now include these fields in your standard logs and deliver them to Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Data Firehose, without setting up an additional data stream for real-time logs. The new fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score. They also include Common Media Client Data (CMCD) fields, which video players send with each request to report details like bitrate, buffer length, and playback session ID. Streaming teams can use these fields to match playback problems that viewers see with CloudFront delivery data, which makes troubleshooting faster. These fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies. To learn more, see Standard logging page in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon CloudFront ajoute à ses journaux standards des champs d'accès auparavant réservés aux journaux en temps réel, dont l'adresse IP du serveur CloudFront, des identifiants distinguant le trafic de distributions principale et de préproduction, un score de confiance sur la qualité média et des champs CMCD envoyés par les lecteurs vidéo (débit, longueur de tampon, identifiant de session). Ces champs peuvent être livrés vers Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs ou Data Firehose sans flux temps réel supplémentaire, ce qui aide au dépannage des problèmes de lecture en diffusion. La tarification standard des journaux s'applique.
articles.title: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports CMCD and additional log fields

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS). Customers can now use TLS certificates to authenticate requests from CloudFront while setting up WebSocket or gRPC connections to their origins. Origin mTLS protects internet facing applications that need persistent, bidirectional or streaming connections, such as chat platforms, collaborative editing tools or live dashboards from unauthenticated requests. Previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront. This was operationally complex and did not provide strong authentication. With Origin mTLS, customers can use one TLS based authentication for HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC traffic to an application origin. This works with application origins within AWS such as Application Load Balancer and API Gateway, on-premises origins, and origins hosted outside AWS. There is no additional charge for origin mTLS, and it is available with pay-as-you-go pricing and in the Business and Premium flat-rate pricing plans. To learn more, visit the CloudFront origin mutual TLS documentation .
articles.title: Amazon CloudFront Announces WebSocket and gRPC Support for Origin Mutual TLS

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances . You can now run GPU-accelerated workloads including AI inference, media processing, 3D rendering, scientific computing, and financial simulations on Lambda without managing GPU drivers, frameworks, or scaling. Lambda runs multiple invocations concurrently in each execution environment and scales responsively based on GPU utilization, CPU utilization, and concurrency to keep your GPUs busy and reduce costs. GPU-accelerated functions integrate with the same 200+ AWS event sources as other Event Functions, so you can add GPU compute as another step in your serverless application. Running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management. With this launch, you can go from code to a running GPU workload in minutes. Lambda provides GPU base images preconfigured with frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch. You can run workloads with large artifacts using container images and NVMe ephemeral storage of up to 32 GB each. To reduce startup time, Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading and streaming artifacts directly from Amazon S3. For resilience, you can select G-series instance types from multiple generations in the allowed instance types for your capacity provider. Lambda provisions instances from the newest generation that meets your function…
articles.title: AWS Lambda adds support for GPU instances on Lambda Managed Instances

articles.excerpt: Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 launches with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer. The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution plans for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes . You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments , in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS User Guide . This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for MySQL is available. Learn more about pricing details at Amazon RDS for MySQL pricing . Amazon RDS for MySQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale MySQL deployments in the cloud. Create or update a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).
articles.title: Amazon RDS for MySQL now supports MySQL major version 9.7

articles.excerpt: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Hybrid Nodes now has lower pricing for large nodes, capping the billed vCPU per node at 32 vCPU, so you are no longer charged for vCPUs above that per node threshold. Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes lets you use your existing on-premises and edge infrastructure as nodes in Amazon EKS clusters. You can now use your largest servers, including those with GPUs, with Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes at lower cost. With this change, the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes cost of a large server no longer grows with its vCPU count. At the first pricing tier, a 64 vCPU node now costs 50% less than before, and a 256 vCPU node costs 88% less, as both are now billed only for 32 vCPUs. This makes Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes more cost-effective for large bare-metal and GPU servers running compute-intensive workloads, such as AI/ML training and inference, that must stay on-premises for data residency, latency, or regulatory reasons. The pricing change applies automatically to all new hybrid nodes. For the new pricing to take effect for existing hybrid nodes attached to clusters, delete and reattach them. Nodes with 32 vCPUs or fewer are still billed for their actual vCPUs, and existing tiered pricing still applies, so your effective rate falls as monthly usage grows. The new pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes is available. To learn more about getting started and updated pricing details, visit the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes documentation and…
articles.title: Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes reduces price for large hosts

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request. CloudFront Functions runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses. Previously, if your logic depended on data from another service, you had to use Lambda@Edge or move that logic to your origin. Now your functions can use real-time data to personalize, authenticate, or route requests at the edge, close to your viewers. With the new cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request. For example, you can check an AI agent's permissions and usage budget so that only authorized requests reach your API or MCP server, or send request signals to a security or fraud detection service to block or challenge bad traffic. With cf.beacon() , you can send analytics events in the background without slowing down viewers, even for content served from cache. articles.excerpt: You can now replicate data in Amazon S3 buckets with fewer replication rules using two new S3 Replication capabilities, exclusions and Multi-Region key resolution. Assessments is an agentic workflow that lets you run automated, isolated synthetic benchmarks on cloned instances, helping you verify potential performance gains before touching your production environment. Moving from recommendations to production changes Managing production databases means balancing system stability, performance, and infrastructure spend. When Database Center alerts you to a potential bottleneck and recommends a change, you need to evaluate the change before you can implement it. That workflow can be complex: Setting up dedicated staging environments to mirror production settings Running benchmark workloads to simulate real-world traffic Measuring latency, throughput, and resource saturation before and after applying changes Calculating whether performance gains justify potential cost adjustments Because this manual benchmarking process takes a lot of time and engineering effort, it’s easy to put off making critical…
articles.summary: Google Cloud annonce la préversion des « assessments » dans Database Center pour Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. Cette fonctionnalité agentique exécute des benchmarks synthétiques isolés sur des instances clonées, afin de vérifier les gains de performance potentiels avant de modifier la base de données de production. Elle vise à réduire le temps et l'effort nécessaires à la mise en place manuelle d'environnements de préproduction.

articles.excerpt: The speed of development in large open-source projects has always been limited by code review, not code generation. Even as coding agents get better at writing code, they do not accelerate development on their own. This is especially true of patches to the Linux kernel. Without a way to build trust in proposed changes, more generated code simply piles up in front of the same small group of human maintainers. Some of those patches are solid changes, just written faster; many others are plausible-looking "AI slop" sent by contributors who do not fully understand the systems they are modifying. And the influx of AI-generated security reports, many of which are duplicates or inaccurate, only adds to maintainers’ load. Linux runs billions of Android phones, most cloud providers, and nearly every supercomputer. It spans more than 35 million lines of code, and over 85,000 changes land every year. Automated build bots and fuzzers like Syzkaller catch build errors and crashes, but code review has always been the main way to guarantee the stability and safety of the kernel. Every day, maintainers read hundreds and hundreds of proposed patches by hand to catch memory leaks, deadlocks, race conditions, and security bugs. To help maintainers handle the load and catch bugs before they land, the Google AI & Infrastructure team built Sashiko , an open-source, agentic code review system powered by Gemini. We named the project after the Japanese word 刺し子, a stitching technique for…
articles.summary: Google a développé Sashiko, un système open source de revue de code agentique propulsé par Gemini, destiné au noyau Linux. Le projet vise à aider les mainteneurs, qui doivent examiner à la main des centaines de correctifs par jour, à détecter fuites de mémoire, interblocages, conditions de course et failles de sécurité avant leur intégration. L'extrait souligne que la revue de code, et non la génération, limite la vitesse de développement de ces projets.
articles.title: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux

articles.excerpt: At Google Cloud, we believe the next generation of AI and agentic systems must be built on open, battle-tested foundations. Envoy, an open-source edge and service proxy designed for cloud-native applications, has already transformed microservices and modern cloud networking, powering everything from Google Cloud’s Application Load Balancers to the Agent Substrate dataplane on Google Kubernetes Engine. Now, Envoy is uniquely positioned to become the open standard for AI traffic, MCP tooling, and agent-to-agent communication. Earlier this year, we presented the technical case for Envoy networking in the agentic AI era , examining how autonomous AI agents fundamentally challenge traditional Layer 7 networking assumptions. Unlike microservices, autonomous agent workloads choose who they communicate with. In addition, their routing attributes live deep within request bodies, with their traffic governed by token budgets as well as request rates, and their multi-turn reasoning loops requiring stateful session affinity and strict tool execution boundaries. At Google Cloud, we have been working hard to develop Envoy for the agentic era. Read on for a closer look at how Envoy has evolved to better support autonomous agents, giving developers the performance and portability of an open-source ecosystem, backed by enterprise security and scalability. articles.summary: Google Cloud présente une évolution d'Envoy, proxy open source déjà utilisé par ses Application Load Balancers et le dataplane Agent Substrate sur GKE, pour en faire un standard ouvert du trafic IA, de l'outillage MCP et de la communication agent-à-agent. articles.excerpt: TL;DR: Single-stack IPv6 on GKE runs both nodes and pods without having to use private IPv4 addresses. Available in preview for Cloud TPU v6e and CPU node pools, including Axion, it works with DNS64/NAT64 to reach IPv4 endpoints. Long before they run out of compute or power, AI applications hit another wall: running out of IP addresses. A single AI deployment often requires a vast address space to support everything from thousands of accelerator nodes, scaling inference replicas, bursting Ray workers and pipelines, pod sidecars, and services like vector databases. Running a dual stack — IPv6 behind a private IPv4 space — can help, but only to a point, because the private IPv4 space has often already been exhausted across existing networks. To help, today, we're announcing single-stack IPv6 on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), allowing you to run both nodes and pods on IPv6, without private IPv4 addresses. Single-stack IPv6 is available in preview for Cloud TPU v6e and CPU node pools, including Axion, and works with DNS64/NAT64 to reach IPv4 endpoints. Nodes and pods run IPv6-only across Cloud TPU v6e and CPU-based node pools, with no private IPv4. Workloads reach Google Cloud APIs over native IPv6 and IPv4-only endpoints through DNS64/NAT64. What single-stack IPv6 delivers The availability of single-stack IPv6 in GKE is a game-changer for large AI deployments. Consider the following features and benefits that it brings to the table: 1. No private IPv4 required for nodes or…
articles.summary: Google Cloud annonce en préversion l'IPv6 en mode pile unique (single-stack) sur Google Kubernetes Engine, permettant aux nœuds et aux pods de fonctionner sans adresses IPv4 privées. Cette option est disponible pour les pools de nœuds Cloud TPU v6e et CPU (dont Axion) et fonctionne avec DNS64/NAT64 pour joindre les points de terminaison IPv4. L'objectif est de répondre à l'épuisement des adresses IP qui limite les grands déploiements d'IA.
articles.title: Scaling massive AI/ML workloads with IPv6 on Google Kubernetes Engine clusters

articles.summary: Talika « Tilly » Stuart, mère à Burlington en Ontario, est décédée des suites d'un incendie résidentiel survenu durant la fin de semaine, selon un ami de la famille. articles.summary: Staples Canada accueillera des rayons Toys "R" Us et Parties "R" Us dans une partie de ses 300 magasins d'ici la fin de l'année prochaine, dans le but de relancer cette marque populaire. articles.title: Toys 'R' Us partnership has Staples Canada playing around with its business model

articles.excerpt: Krampus may have been banned from a Santa Claus parade in southern Ontario, but the European folklore creature is expected to make appearances at several festive events in Thunder Bay. Here's why people in Thunder Bay can't get enough of Krampus.
articles.summary: Krampus, créature du folklore européen mi-chèvre mi-démon associée à la punition des enfants turbulents, a été interdit d'un défilé du Père Noël dans une ville du sud de l'Ontario. Il devrait toutefois faire plusieurs apparitions lors d'événements des fêtes à Thunder Bay.

articles.excerpt: Saskatchewan's First Nations Health Ombudsperson is investigating how a Regina boy lost his small intestine after a routine surgery for appendicitis.

articles.excerpt: Hundreds of students at New Brunswick high schools walked out Wednesday afternoon to protest against the coming broader ban on cellphones in schools.
articles.summary: Des centaines d'élèves d'écoles secondaires du Nouveau-Brunswick ont quitté leurs classes mercredi après-midi pour protester contre l'interdiction élargie des téléphones cellulaires dans les écoles, qui doit entrer en vigueur prochainement. Il s'agit d'un événement régional sans portée nationale évidente pour ce lecteur.
articles.title: High school students across N.B. walk out over cellphone ban

digest.text: Trump, Xi et Poutine se sont réunis à Shenzhen, en marge de l'APEC, pour une rencontre trilatérale inédite. Ils ont adopté une « déclaration de paix » et évoqué l'Ukraine, le nucléaire, le pétrole et la réforme de l'ONU.

Anthropic a fait ses débuts au Nasdaq (ANT) à 83 $, levant environ 80 milliards US, un record, puis a bondi d'environ 34 %. Sa valorisation approche 2000 milliards US, avec des effets pour les caisses de retraite et les banques.

Une faille d'authentification critique de VMware vCenter (CVSS 9,8) est exploitée par l'acteur lié à la Chine ARMORY CASTLE, et des correctifs existent. Apache Roller, NGINX et PHP présentent aussi des failles d'exécution de code à distance.

Une cyberattaque assistée par l'IA a visé la Commission européenne, qui a mis hors ligne des systèmes internes. Equinor, KPMG Canada et N-able signalent aussi des intrusions, ce qui souligne la pression sur les organisations.

Selon l'AIE, la consommation d'électricité des centres de données pourrait doubler d'ici 2030 avec l'essor de l'IA. Son rapport prévient aussi que le conflit au Moyen-Orient laissera une trace durable sur l'énergie.
Selon le Globe and Mail, Québecor aurait fait une offre d'achat pour Telus, et Bell aurait entamé des discussions avec Telus. Québecor juge qu'une prise de contrôle par BCE nuirait aux consommateurs.
Ubisoft supprime 166 emplois au Québec, 128 à Montréal et 38 à Québec, quelques heures avant ses résultats trimestriels. Le contexte demeure morose pour l'entreprise.
